analysis.title: HF Sinclair Corp. (DINO): 3Q Recap: Strong Results Driven by Refining; Focus on Lubes Transaction, Capital Returns & Strategic Initiatives; Buy
key_insights: DINO reported 3Q26 results stronger than GS anticipated, driven by refining, where capture rate was about 105% excluding benefits related to small refinery exemptions (SREs).
DINO named Steve Ledbetter CEO and President effective Jan. 1, 2027, which GS views as a positive tailwind for the stock.

GS notes YTD outperformance and says relative valuation is the main pushback in investor conversations. GS also wants more detail on cash flow and earnings effects of the Lubricants spin-off and the Westline Connect project.
GS keeps a Buy rating and cuts the 6-month price target to $138 from $142. It sees 23.3% upside from $111.89 and potential for positive consensus earnings revisions.

Management is constructive on refining, citing tight global product inventories and constrained capacity. About 4 mb/d of refining capacity is offline globally, roughly 2.5 mb/d in the Middle East and 1.5 mb/d in Russia.

The system can run about 100 kb/d of heavy crude, with WCS a substantial portion. DINO expects WCS differentials to keep widening near term on Canadian production outpacing pipeline egress, higher international freight rates and incremental Venezuelan crude on the Gulf Coast.
Management expects WCS differentials of $25-$30/bbl to moderate over time but to stay wider than historical levels through at least 2027.

4Q26 refining crude throughput is guided to 560-600 kb/d, reflecting a planned El Dorado turnaround. A vacuum-furnace project there is expected to add about 10 kb/d of heavy crude capacity and improve product yields.
Full-year 2026 capex guidance was revised to about $725 mn for sustaining capital and turnarounds plus $150 mn of growth capital (Western Gateway, Westline Connect, marketing joint ventures).
Management is not actively pursuing M&A and is focused on high-return organic projects in midstream, marketing and refining reliability.

The Lubricants separation remains on track for 2H2027. Work now covers securing the PLR, preparing the Form 10 and filling key leadership roles. The goal is full standalone operational readiness by early 3Q27, and NewCo is to launch with a strong, flexible balance sheet.

Westline Connect first-phase FID moved to 1Q27 from 4Q26. Phase one adds about 35 kb/d of product supply from the Rockies into Utah/Nevada, targets an online date in 2029, and is to be funded with cash on hand and operating cash flow. GS says it complements Western Gateway for PADD 5 supply.

In Renewable Fuels, more than 50% of product sales now go outside California, with placement in the Pacific Northwest, Canada and New Mexico. Management also credits advantaged feedstock sourcing and operating expense discipline.
GS's 4Q26 EPS estimate is $7.50 versus FactSet consensus of $6.25. Its 2026-2028 EPS estimates are $25.24/$15.41/$8.78, versus $20.03/$14.92/$8.75 before.

market_movers.rationale: GS lowers the 6-month price target to $138 from $142 on a 12.0x P/E on normalized EPS and a sum-of-the-parts valuation. It cites the refining beat, a possible positive revision cycle and non-refining earnings durability, and notes relative valuation pushback after YTD outperformance.

sector_views.rationale: Management cites tight global product inventories, about 4 mb/d of capacity offline and constrained refining capacity. GS likes DINO's niche refining markets and non-refining earnings.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported: refining capture rate about 105% excluding SRE impacts, described by GS as stronger than anticipated. The report gives no 3Q26 EPS figure.
4Q26 EPS: GS estimate $7.50 versus FactSet consensus $6.25 (both estimates, not printed).
GS EPS estimates, new versus old: 2026E $25.24 vs $20.03, 2027E $15.41 vs $14.92, 2028E $8.78 vs $8.75. 2025 actual EPS was $3.79.
GS quarterly EPS path: 3Q26 (9/26) $11.75, 4Q26E $7.50, 1Q27E $3.25, 2Q27E $4.06. The report does not say whether the 9/26 figure is reported or estimated.
GS 2026E revenue $35,864.8 mn (old $35,365.6 mn) and 2026E EBITDA $6,783.7 mn. 2027E revenue $33,468.3 mn and EBITDA $4,233.1 mn.
4Q26 refining crude throughput guidance is 560-600 kb/d, reflecting the El Dorado turnaround.
risk_factors: Unclear cash flow and earnings effects of the Lubricants spin-off and the Westline Connect project, including the FID delay to 1Q27.
geopolitical: Refining capacity offline of about 4 mb/d globally, about 2.5 mb/d in the Middle East and about 1.5 mb/d in Russia, supports product inventories and margins per management.
Incremental Venezuelan crude on the Gulf Coast is cited as a driver of wider WCS differentials.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees attractive risk/reward and potential for positive consensus earnings revisions. Its 4Q26 EPS estimate of $7.50 is above FactSet consensus of $6.25, and it likes niche refining exposure, non-refining earnings, balance sheet strength and SRE optionality.
tension_points.bear_case: GS notes YTD outperformance, with relative valuation the main investor pushback. Cash flow and earnings effects of the Lubricants spin-off and Westline Connect remain unclear.
